problem: The sentence 'The first user process is started by PID 1, which is init or systemd on modern systems' contradicts itself. PID 1 is itself the first user-space process; the kernel starts it, not another process. A student will read this as 'something with PID 1 starts init', which is wrong.
fix: PID 1 is init, or systemd on modern systems. The kernel starts it directly as the first user-space process, and every other process is created by a parent process, so a tree of PIDs and PPIDs forms below PID 1.

where: Worked example 1, steps 4-6, and quiz Q3
problem: The answer says the process disappears with no STAT at all. In Linux the entry stays visible as STAT Z (zombie) from the moment it dies until its parent collects the exit status. An interactive shell usually reaps in microseconds, but on a busy or non-interactive parent a student who re-runs ps will see Z and think the book is wrong.
fix: Add one line: after the signal the process dies at once, but it can show STAT Z for a short time until its parent collects the exit status; the shell normally does this so fast that ps shows no row. Q3 answer: the process is terminated; it may show STAT Z briefly, then no row remains.

problem: 'then stop the process with SIGTERM' uses 'stop' for 'terminate'. The chapter has already defined stopped as STAT T (Ctrl-Z, SIGTSTP), so this wording clashes with its own definition.
fix: 'then terminate the process with SIGTERM and, if it is still alive after 5 s, with SIGKILL.'

problem: 'only root can set a negative value' is incomplete. A normal user can only raise the nice value (lower the priority); lowering it at all, even from 10 to 5, also needs root or the CAP_SYS_NICE capability. As written, a student would expect renice -n 5 on their own process at nice 10 to succeed.
fix: 'The range is -20 (highest CPU priority) to 19 (lowest). A normal user can only raise the nice value of a process (make it lower priority); lowering it, including setting a negative value, needs root.'

where: Section 1, foreground and background jobs paragraph
problem: 'A background job runs without the terminal prompt' is unclear. The prompt does come back; what the job lacks is the terminal's foreground process group.
fix: 'A background job is started with & ; the shell prompt returns at once and the job runs without owning the terminal, so Ctrl-C and Ctrl-Z do not reach it.'

problem: The question asks to 'list job 2' but the answer gives plain jobs, which lists all jobs, not job 2.
fix: Answer: jobs %2 lists job 2, bg %2 resumes it in the background, fg %2 brings it to the foreground. (Plain jobs is acceptable only if the question says 'list the jobs'.)

problem: 'A check with ps -p 4242 shows no row' is slightly off: ps still prints the header line (PID TTY TIME CMD) and only the data row is missing, which confuses students looking at the screen.
fix: 'ps -p 4242 then prints only the header line, with no data row for 4242.'
